title: I am scared that no one will play my game because it is made with AI
author: Guilty-Manner219
selftext:
I have put over 1000+ hours to make this pc game. But neither I am a game artist nor I have a budget to get people to do the artwork or voice or music for the game, I have used AI. Now I am shit scared that no one will ever download it because of the AI declaration we have to post on steam store page. And thus i am releasing the game as Free to Play.

My main aim to make this game was to convey a pretty cool story I thought in the form of a two-part game(platformer puzzle).

**Is it normal to feel the shame/guilt or am i overthinking?**

Btw if anyone’s interested here is the story of the game.  
The world changed in 2037, when an entity called **Consensus** took control of humanity.

Consensus can control the minds of every human. Over the years, it made everyone live inside one massive building called Takarek, a building with 17,769 floors.

It is now 2077.

**You play as Alex**, a 20 year old Deprecation Clerk. Your job is to review old and unused data and delete it forever.

It is just another night at work, until you receive a **mysterious letter**:

DON'T LET RK-001 BE DELETED.  
IT'S THE ONLY WAY OUT OF TAKAREK.

You don't know who sent the letter. You don't know what RK-001 is. But you decide to find out.

What starts as a normal night at work slowly turns into a journey through the hidden parts of Takarek. You will discover forgotten information, strange clues, secrets from the past, and the truth about Consensus.

And somehow, you may be the only person who can stop it.

The world belongs to Consensus.  
But tonight, you have one chance to change that.

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5266980/RaviWar\_1\_A\_Perfect\_Sonday/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5266980/RaviWar_1_A_Perfect_Sonday/)

replies.author: HippieYoHippieYay
replies.body:
Meh, sorry 🤷‍♂️

The repeat thought it kept conveying is "Oh, it's just another generic X", just seemed like a bunch of random mechanics cobbled together.

I'm sure that there's a grand story and all that jazz that is supposed to hold everything together, but the truth is that most players don't care about any of that stuff, only the gameplay and gameloop matter. 

If you remove all the decoration and replace all your models with capsules, is the game actually fun or just generic feeling? 


Gamers have a limited amount of time to play, so you always have to think what would make them choose YOUR game over their current go-to game. What makes your game stand out? What is the actual novelty? What's the single best mechanic or selling point of your game, and put that in your trailer first.

Story and setting don't matter, your marketing has to communicate why this game is "more fun" than the one I was already having fun playing.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
Imo, ppl sometimes overestimate how much impact AI disclosure has VS how much impact oversaturation and other factors have.  
  
For indie games AI disclosure covers, let say, 10% of failures, and 90% of consists of being "one out of gazzilions games released every month", players not having enough time, game being obscure and unknown, overall lower quality, game presentation not catching interest, stale genre, clone vibes and many other things. 

Like in order to get anti-AI pushback one has to get at least some views\\discussions going on.    
Majority of indie games don\`t get that at all, because there is not enough "gaming hours" on the market to cover all games...

Dev who uses AI will deffo run into this more often due to faster production speed, but at the end of the day - the amount of ppl who will not play his game purely due to AI - is fixed and limited, while the amount of ppl who will not play for different reasons - is flexible and adjustable, and it varies on the product, marketing, trends and so on.

comments.author: YYS770
comments.body:
Just took a look.   
Ignoring the raging anti-ai mob, if I'm sharing my own perspective as someone who doesn't have an ethical problem with ai-use, the thing that will turn me off relating to AI, is if the thumbnail looks like it was AI generated, that would tel lme that if not enough effort was put into the FRONT PAGE AND FACE of your game, it's likely that the game isn't worth playing either. 

But your thumbnail doesn't tell me that. 

However, I will say that your trailer, images, and gameplay footage tells me absolutely nothing about what your game is, what to expect, and so on. These things should at least give me an idea of what fun experiences to expect, to draw me in.   
To that end, i would HEAVILY recommend you to avoid at all costs including images and footage of the arcade minigames. these things are supposed to be bonuses within the game, but it does your marketing harm IMO by drawing attention away from your core game and towards something that seemingly has nothing to do with it. Makes your core game look weaker for a variety of reasons. 

there are also a few parts of the trailer whcih I think do harm - like when the floor-panels-puzzle-thing shows you moving forward and then backward, the screen jumps frames all over the place. it's not clear if that's a bug, or intentional, and if it is indeed intentional then it's not clear why it would look like that. 

In short, try to think of a through-line that you're taking the audience on when seeing your trailer. What's fun about this game? pictures of the lovely ceiling and beautiful water texture outside of any context does not sell me a fun experience, nor does it tell me why your game is FUN. 

Good luck!

comments.author: KevinDL
comments.body:
I don’t think you should be worried about the AI disclosure.

If you want honest feedback, I looked at the Steam page and watched the trailer. The bigger issue is that the game itself isn’t selling me on why I should play it.

Visually, it feels very generic and inconsistent. The different assets and styles don’t feel like they belong to the same game, and nothing immediately gives it a strong visual identity. More importantly, after watching the trailer, I still don’t really understand what I’m supposed to do as a player or what makes the gameplay interesting. That’s a much bigger problem than an AI disclosure.

I’m saying this as someone who works professionally in this space: based purely on what is currently on the Steam page, I wouldn't expect this game to perform particularly well. That has very little to do with AI. It just doesn’t look compelling yet.

And the 1,000+ hours you’ve spent making it unfortunately doesn’t change that. Players don’t know whether something took 100 hours, 1,000 hours, or 10,000 hours to make. The market doesn’t reward development time or effort. It responds to the thing you actually put in front of people.

Some people will refuse to play a game because it uses generative AI, and you have to accept you’ve lost that audience. But plenty of people don’t care, as long as the result is good.

So I wouldn’t release it for free because you’re ashamed of using AI. If anything, I’d take a hard look at the game and its presentation and ask: **If nobody knew or cared how this was made, would this trailer make them want to play it?**

Right now, I think that’s the problem you need to solve.
